Read the passage and answer the questions.

In a school of 800 students, 45% are girls.

(i) How many girls are there?
(ii) How many boys?
(iii) If 10% of the girls and 20% of the boys play cricket, how many in total play cricket?
(iv) What percent of the total student body plays cricket?

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A shopkeeper buys a TV at ₹15000 and marks it 20% above cost.

(i) What is the marked price?
(ii) If he allows a 10% discount on the marked price, what is the selling price?
(iii) What is his profit (or loss) and the profit % ?
(iv) What would be the SP if no discount were given?

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A store offers two successive discounts: 20% and then 10% on the discounted price.

(i) For an item marked ₹500, find the price after the first discount.
(ii) Find the price after the second discount.
(iii) What single discount % would give the same final price?
(iv) Why is the single equivalent discount NOT 30%?
questions.answer:
(i) After 20%: 500 × 0.8 = ₹400.
(ii) After further 10%: 400 × 0.9 = ₹360.
(iii) Single discount = (500 − 360)/500 × 100 = 140/500 × 100 = 28%.
(iv) Because the second discount applies to the ALREADY REDUCED price (₹400), not the original (₹500). 30% would be adding two flat reductions on the same base.

Read the passage and answer the questions.

Priya deposits ₹10000 at a bank offering 6% per annum simple interest.

(i) Find the interest earned in 1 year.
(ii) Find the interest earned in 3 years.
(iii) Find the total amount after 3 years.
(iv) After how many years will the interest equal ₹3000?

Read the passage and answer the questions.

A sum of ₹8000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.

(i) State the CI formula.
(ii) Compute the amount after 3 years.
(iii) Compute the compound interest earned.
(iv) Compute the simple interest at the same rate and period; compare.
questions.answer:
(i) A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.
(ii) A = 8000 × (1.1)³ = 8000 × 1.331 = ₹10648.
(iii) CI = 10648 − 8000 = ₹2648.
(iv) SI = (8000 × 10 × 3)/100 = ₹2400. CI − SI = ₹248. CI > SI because the interest itself earns interest in subsequent years.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A bottle's price is increased by 10%, then the increased price is decreased by 10%.

(i) Let original = ₹100. Find the price after the increase.
(ii) Find the price after the subsequent decrease.
(iii) What is the net change as a percentage of the original?
(iv) Generalise: if a value is increased by x% then decreased by x%, what is the net change?
questions.answer:
(i) After 10% increase: 100 × 1.10 = ₹110.
(ii) After 10% decrease on the new price: 110 × 0.90 = ₹99.
(iii) Change = 99 − 100 = −1 ⇒ −1% (a 1% net DECREASE).
(iv) Net = (1 + x/100)(1 − x/100) − 1 = −(x/100)² = −x²/10000. So a net DECREASE of x²/100 percent. For x = 10: 1% decrease ✓.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

The population of a village was 8000 last year. It increased to 8800 this year.

(i) Find the percentage growth.
(ii) If the growth continues at the same rate, what will the population be next year?
(iii) After how many more years will it cross 12000? (Use approximate calculations.)
(iv) Is this kind of growth simple or compound? Justify.
questions.answer:
(i) Growth = 800/8000 × 100 = 10%.
(ii) Next year: 8800 × 1.10 = 9680.
(iii) Need P > 12000. Starting from 8800: 8800 × (1.10)ⁿ > 12000 ⇒ (1.10)ⁿ > 12000/8800 ≈ 1.364. Try n = 4: 1.1⁴ ≈ 1.464. n = 3: 1.331. So between 3 and 4 years. So population first crosses 12000 after about 4 more years from this year.
(iv) Compound — each year's growth applies to the latest population, not the original (8000). Successive multiplication, not addition.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

In a survey, 60% of people prefer tea, 30% prefer coffee, and the remaining 30 people prefer neither.

(i) Let total = T. Express the number preferring neither in terms of T.
(ii) Set up an equation.
(iii) Solve for T.
(iv) How many prefer tea?
questions.answer:
(i) Tea = 60% = 0.6T. Coffee = 30% = 0.3T. Neither = 10% = 0.1T.
(ii) 0.1T = 30.
(iii) T = 300.
(iv) Tea drinkers = 0.6 × 300 = 180.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

A dealer buys 50 books for ₹3000 and sells them at ₹80 each.

(i) Find the cost price of one book.
(ii) Find the selling price of one book.
(iii) Find profit per book and the total profit.
(iv) Find profit %.
questions.answer:
(i) CP per book = 3000/50 = ₹60.
(ii) SP per book = ₹80.
(iii) Profit per book = 80 − 60 = ₹20. Total profit = 50 × 20 = ₹1000.
(iv) Profit % = (20/60) × 100 = 33.33%.
